newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, low sulphur fuel falls $5.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, low sulphur fuel falls $5.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Wednesday as low sulphur fuel oil lost $5, traders said.
Gas oil was unchanged but premiums for Russian 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil slipped slightly with the emergence of fresh Black Sea supply.
Six cargoes of 25,000 to 30,000 tonnes each were due to come onto the market loading Jan 16-25 from Novorosiisk and Tuapse.
Traders said the additional supply was likely to depress premiums to around cif high quotes +$1.50 basis Genoa from Tuesday's traded level of +$1.60 and last week's +$2 .

Interest in the Med in low sulphur diesel remains dormant but the product was supported by interest from NWE, with a French major seeking 20,000 tonnes into Le Havre for Jan 23-28. A European major was rumoured to have sold a large cargo of low sulphur from Lavera to a European trader for Indian end-users but numbers did not emerge.
Naphtha continues to move transatlantic despite a dearth of tonnage which has prompted high freight rates.
Reformer grade naphtha was becoming harder to source.
Prices were a touch stronger at $226-220 cif Med, taking a cue from firmer numbers in NWE.

Gasoline was slow, although 5,000 tonnes of demand was seen into Italy with material available in Italy and France. Prices were buffeted by easier U.S. numbers, but recovered during the course of the day as NYMEX retraced losses.

Low sulphur fuel oil fell hard. Offers into Italy were $3 weaker at $127 cif Milazzo for late Jan/early Feb. A regular buyer said he saw 200,000 tonnes of low sulphur available from Europe in January, with the possibility of more from America.
High sulphur prices held their strength better, and swaps were talked at around $112/$114 fob Med.
